title: Error Handling Patterns
summary: How C programs report and recover from failure - return codes and out-parameters, errno with strerror and perror, an error enum with messages, cleaning up with a single goto exit, assert for programmer mistakes, and setjmp and longjmp for jumping out of deep calls.

cards.q: Why copy `errno` straight after the failing call?
cards.a:
The next library call, even a successful one like `printf`, may change it

Library functions may set `errno` even when they succeed, so save it in a local before calling anything else.

cards.q: Why are the cleanup labels in reverse order of acquiring?
cards.a:
A jump frees exactly what was acquired so far

Each label frees one resource and falls into the next. A failure at step N jumps to the label for step N − 1, so exactly the earlier resources are freed, newest first.

cards.q: Which should never be checked with assert?
cards.a:
whether malloc returned NULL

malloc can fail in a correct program, and assert disappears with NDEBUG: it needs real handling.
